title: A Cipher for the Deadline
premise: Mara Yarrow, a freelance interpreter embedded with the Halvern peace delegation, has spent years cultivating anonymity as armor—until Flight 447, carrying the delegation's chief negotiator, vanishes from every radar and manifest while still airborne. The disappearance is no accident but a coordinated erasure orchestrated by a cabal inside the security consortium meant to protect the talks, timed to trigger a 'catastrophic malfunction' that will bury the peace process and its inconvenient witnesses. Mara's polished lie—that she was never really there—unravels when she realizes her own interpretation notes contain the cipher key to the attack schedule. Racing a dawn extraction flight that doubles as the kill window, she allies with a disgraced air-traffic investigator and a delegation aide who may be a plant, trading her invisibility for justice the law cannot deliver. In the end she exposes the conspiracy by broadcasting the erased flight's true record, chooses exile over erasure, and finally belongs—to the truth, if to nothing else.
about_author: Isandro Underhill is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in negotiation rooms across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose professions demand they be heard but never seen.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Mara Yarrow's POV. In a lakeside hotel hosting fragile peace talks, Mara rehearses her cover story, checks her go-bag, and interprets a tense preliminary session where negotiator Elias Voss hints someone is sabotaging the process. Emotional beat: controlled paranoia—the comfort of routines built for escape.

chapters.title: Protocol of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She smooths over a mistranslation that nearly derails a session, drawing the attention of delegation aide Tomas Reyes, who asks too many friendly questions. That night she finds her hotel room searched with surgical precision. Emotional beat: the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Voss departs on a midnight shuttle to fetch a holdout minister; Mara watches from the tarmac, translating his final radio check. Forty minutes later, the tower has no record the flight ever existed. Emotional beat: vertigo—the world editing itself while she watches.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara and investigator Dara Okonkwo's POVs. Dara, suspended from the aviation authority for asking wrong questions, notices the same void in the radar archive. The two meet hostilely at the authority's offices, each suspecting the other. Emotional beat: two loners recognizing a shared wound.

chapters.title: What the Delegation Knew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The delegation leadership insists Voss never boarded, producing immaculate paperwork—and Mara's own signed attendance log has been altered. Tomas warns her to stop digging. Emotional beat: gaslit dread; her one skill, precision with words, is being turned against her.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Notebook
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Dara obtains Mara's seized notebooks and discovers her shorthand notation system maps frequencies and timings no interpreter should care about. She confronts Mara; instead of betrayal, they find the outline of a schedule hidden in the delegation's own terminology. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Consortium
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Director Hale of Meridian Security). Hale reviews the operation: the flight was diverted, passengers held, and the 'accident' scheduled for dawn to coincide with an extraction flight carrying evidence out of the country. Emotional beat: chilling bureaucratic calm—evil as logistics.

chapters.title: A Cipher in Plain Speech
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Decoding her own notes, Mara realizes the delegation's negotiating vocabulary was engineered as a cipher—she has been transmitting the attack schedule without knowing it. Every session she interpreted was a countdown. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tests Tomas with a false detail; he passes it to Meridian within the hour. Confronted, he confesses he was planted years ago but has been feeding the resistance fragments. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness tangled—belonging offered by a liar.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes of Static
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Dara traces the missing ninety minutes of radar data to a private relay station and recovers a corrupted fragment: Flight 447 landed alive at a decommissioned airstrip. Emotional beat: hope with a timer attached.

chapters.title: The Airstrip
chapters.summary: Mara and Dara's POV, alternating. They reach the airstrip, find the passengers drugged but alive under guard, and are spotted escaping with photographic proof—and a wounded pilot who confirms the dawn 'malfunction' plan. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Hunted Interpreters
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Meridian brands them terrorists; their faces hit security feeds. Mara uses her knowledge of protocol, checkpoints, and language to slip the net, teaching Dara her tradecraft. Emotional beat: her invisible-life skills become weapons at last.

chapters.title: The Minister Who Waited
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The holdout minister Voss went to fetch is found—and reveals Voss suspected the sabotage and hid the full cipher key with the only person he trusted: Mara. Emotional beat: grief and vindication; she was chosen, not overlooked.

chapters.title: Countdown in Two Languages
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Decoding completes: the extraction flight at dawn will broadcast a falsified distress signal, then vanish like 447, killing everyone aboard and closing the case forever. Hours remain. Emotional beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: Inside Meridian
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas returns to Meridian as a double agent, buying access to the relay station while knowing Hale suspects him. He transmits the control codes to Mara. Emotional beat: a traitor choosing, finally, which side to betray.

chapters.title: The Tower at Night
chapters.summary: Mara and Dara's POV. They seize the relay station; Dara fights the technical battle to restore the erased flight record while guards close in. Mara holds the door, literally and figuratively. Emotional beat: two outsiders defending each other's competence.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With minutes left, Mara does what she was made for: she translates—broadcasting the restored record and decoded schedule in three languages to every newsroom, embassy, and open frequency. Emotional beat: voice as liberation; invisibility abandoned.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The extraction flight, exposed, is grounded by international order; Hale attempts manual override and is arrested mid-transmission as delegates storm the airstrip and free Flight 447's passengers. Emotional beat: catharsis—the machine of power jammed by its own signals.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the inquiry, Mara interprets for the survivors—including Voss—watching her own words become official record. Justice works slowly, imperfectly, but in the open. Emotional beat: weary satisfaction; the law, nudged, catches up.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Offered reinstatement, honors, and a safe posting, Mara realizes visibility has a price: she can never work anonymous rooms again. Tomas leaves quietly; Dara asks her to stay. Emotional beat: bittersweet choice between safety and self.

chapters.title: The Unpacked Bag
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara unpacks the go-bag item by item, keeping only her notebook—the cipher that saved them. She accepts Dara's offer to consult on the investigation, her first standing commitment in years. Emotional beat: quiet transformation; roots where there were only exits.

chapters.title: A Cipher for the Deadline
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Mara's POV. Months later, Mara interprets at the resumed peace talks—not hidden behind glass this time, but named in the program. When a junior interpreter panics, Mara steadies her with the old rules, then adds a new one: make sure someone knows your name. Emotional beat: belonging earned, vigilance kept.
